title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): X is a set, I is an ordered set, and (X_i)_{i∈I} is a family of subsets with i≤j ⇒ X_i⊂X_j. For each i, the 'boundary' is ∂X_i = ∪_{j<i} X_j and the 'open cell' is X_i° = X_i \ ∂X_i. Conditions in play: 2') the X_i° are pairwise disjoint for i≠j; 3') X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j°; (ii) X_i∩X_j = ∪_{k≤i,j} X_k for all i,j. The page proves (i)⇔(ii) inside a proposition characterising when such a family is a 'figure ensembliste' (rigid set-theoretic figure) indexed by I. Combined with Cor. 2 on the previous page, this amounts to a combinatorial model of closed cells: a stratification by disjoint open strata whose closures are unions of lower strata.

(i)⇒(ii): The inclusion ⊃ is clear from monotonicity. For ⊂, write X_i = ∪_{i'≤i} X_{i'}° and X_j = ∪_{j'≤j} X_{j'}° using 3'). Then X_i∩X_j = ∪ X_{i'}°∩X_{j'}°. By 2') only the terms with i'=j'=k survive, and such k satisfy k≤i,j. Hence X_i∩X_j = ∪_{k≤i,j} X_k° ⊂ ∪_{k≤i,j} X_k.

(ii)⇒(i), stated as a Lemma (first called 'Corollaire', then corrected): assume (ii).
- Proof of 2'): take i≠j. Every k≤i,j satisfies k<i or k<j, so X_k⊂∂X_i or X_k⊂∂X_j. Hence X_i∩X_j ⊂ ∂X_i∪∂X_j, which lies in the complement of X_i°∩X_j°. But X_i°∩X_j° ⊂ X_i∩X_j, so X_i°∩X_j° = ∅.
- Proof of 3'): this needs the extra hypothesis, added in the margin, that ∪_i X_i° covers |𝔓|. The inclusion ⊃ is trivial. For ⊂, let x∈X_i; then x∈X_j° for some j, and it suffices to show X_j°∩X_i≠∅ ⇒ j≤i. This is finished on the next page: X_j°∩X_i ⊂ ∪_{k≤i,j} X_k. If j≰i, every such k is <j, so the union lies in ∂X_j, which is disjoint from X_j°. That contradicts nonemptiness.

The purpose is the foundations of a set-theoretic/combinatorial 'analysis situs' (tame-topology programme): characterising poset-indexed families of closed cells, essentially the face-poset structure of regular cell decompositions.
errors: The ⊃ inclusion in (ii), called 'évident', uses the standing hypothesis that i↦X_i is increasing; this is implicit, not stated on the page.
The Lemma as first written claims 3') from (ii) alone. The covering hypothesis ∪X_i° = |𝔓| is genuinely needed and was added only as a marginal correction; otherwise the argument is correct.
In the 2') argument the chain 'X_i°∩X_j° ⊂ ∁(X_i°∩X_j°)' is written loosely, but the logic is sound.

ideas.what: Characterising poset-indexed families of subsets as 'closed cells' by the intersection formula X_i∩X_j = ∪_{k≤i,j} X_k, equivalently disjoint open strata X_i° with X_i = ∪_{j≤i} X_j°.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification satisfying the frontier condition; face-poset / cellular (regular CW-type) decomposition; poset-stratified sets (Alexandrov-topology viewpoint)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Whitney/Thom stratification theory; Björner on regular CW posets; Lurie / Ayala–Francis–Tanaka on poset-stratified spaces)
ideas.where_published: Only programmatic hints in Esquisse d'un programme (§5, tame topology); the 1986 Analysis situs notes are unpublished.

ideas.what: Proof that pairwise disjointness of open cells plus the covering property follow from the intersection formula, via ∂X_i = ∪_{j<i} X_j.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct but elementary lemma in the set-theoretic foundations of Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 Analysis situs. It is interesting as documentation of his tame-topology project, but the mathematics is standard combinatorics of stratifications and face posets.
transcription_corrections: '(côté ⊃ est évident)' – the image reads 'côté ⊃ est évident', consistent with the transcription.
'X_{i'}°∩X_{j'}°=∅ sauf [?] si i'=j'' – image shows 'sauf' followed by the line break 'si i'=j''.
Margin note: 'Si de plus ∪_{i∈I} X_i° = |𝔓|' (|𝔓| as on the previous page, not |X|), followed by 'on a aussi 3')'.
Garbled passage '(les dimensions [?] mises [?], ...' should read roughly: 'et (les k ≤ i,j sont ou bien <i, ou bien <j, à cause que i≠j) donc il en est pour chacun X_k ⊂ ∂X_i ou X_k ⊂ ∂X_j'.
The bottom marginal line reads approximately 'On a bien évidemment ⊃, il faut voir ⊂' (referring to 3')).
